30GB of gp3 storage adds $2.70/month, and I'm checking whether the DynamoDB 20 RCU/20 WCU provisioned capacity falls under the free tier, since AWS covers up to 25 units of read/write capacity continuously — working through whether that threshold translates to roughly 18,600 unit-hours per month (25 units × 744 hours), which would mean the 20 RCU and 20 WCU usage here is fully covered and costs $0.

I'll settle on 730 hrs/month as the standard average for EC2/EBS calculations, while noting that DynamoDB's RCU/WCU usage stays under the free tier threshold regardless of whether the month has 730 or 744 hours, so that cost remains $0. Tallying up: EC2 instance comes to $65.70 and EBS gp3 30GB storage adds $2.70.

This gives a total of roughly $68.40/month, which I'll present along with the key assumptions used (730 hrs/month, on-demand Linux pricing, provisioned capacity within free tier at 20 units each), flagging that the rates are synthetic test fixture values rather than real AWS pricing. | `LedgerIndex` (DynamoDB) | 20 RCU provisioned | free tier: first 25 units/month free | **$0.00** |
